conviction_note: The Q4 bar (~$1.97-2.00 EPS) sits on the company's own +$40-50m sequential core EBITDA guide, so the quarter is mostly pre-told. The stock trades on the next-quarter outlook: CMC has sold three of its last four outlooks. Peer guidance (NUE/STLD, 2026-09-17) is constructive on price and margin, and the sector reset was already taken on 09-18 (-3.8%). Scrap is expected to rise in October and rebar increases are being capped by imports, which argues for a cautious Q1 FY27 guide. These offset, so p_up 48 and abs_move 5.0 (the option-implied move; the chain is wide). impact_sum +0.3 and impact_scaled -0.2 are both near zero; the small sign gap is the downside skew and the outlook-selling history, which sit in p_up and not in any one finding.
bar: Q4 FY26 adj EPS ~$1.97 on ~$2.45bn revenue (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CMC) and $2.00 on $2.54bn (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/earnings-forecasts). Both are consistent with the company guide of core EBITDA up sequentially from $353.6m (8-K 2026-06-25, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm). On the call the CFO put that at roughly +$40-50m (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). TipRanks shows $1.71-1.72, which looks stale or misaligned and was not used. The Q3 bar itself was disputed ($1.60 Zacks vs $1.77 elsewhere), so the reaction to a 'beat' is noisy.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,310,209 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~5.7% of shares outstanding, 5.16 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest, per sweep). That is up from ~4.7m and 3.6 days at 2026-07-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/), a ~34% build into the print. Moderate, not crowded. Skew is +13.54 vol points (25d put minus call): downside paid. But front-expiry OI is only 495 contracts and the ATM spread is 62% of mid, so the skew and the 5.03% implied move are indicative only. Put/call OI is 0.39. Spot $64.74: -22% from the 52w high, -1.65% over 20d, +2.35% over 5d.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call (2026-06-25) the CFO guided Q4 core EBITDA up about $40-50m sequentially from $353.6m (to roughly $394-404m). The guide relies on metal margin recovering to pre-Q3 levels (Q2 $623/t against Q3 $610/t) as announced price increases take hold, and management admitted 'some market discounting'. ChemAnalyst (2026-08-20) says US rebar was range-bound through the quarter: +0.96% in July, -0.94% on 7 Aug on rising import availability, then flat, which risks a partial margin recovery. Nucor's 2026-09-17 guide of higher realized pricing across all major product categories is a broader series pointing the other way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June 2026: Q3 EBITDA +78.6% y/y with a mixed EPS read; the stock moved +3.94% (baseline), so reported-quarter quality has not driven large moves. The big moves (-7.26% Oct 2025, -3.56% Jan 2026, -4.69% Mar 2026) came with the outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.97-2.00 already assumes the full $40-50m step-up. If the market doubted the margin recovery, Q4 estimates would sit nearer $1.85-1.90 (Zacks' stale July number) than at or above guide. They do not.
findings.independence: Guide and discounting comment from the Q3 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). The price trail is a secondary trade-press proxy, not a CMC number. Nucor's guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000073309/000119312526318190/d468854dex991.htm, via the steelorbis 2026-09-17 summary) points the other way.

findings.finding: Two direct long-products peers guided on 2026-09-17, after CMC last spoke. Steel Dynamics expects steel profitability 'significantly higher' sequentially on metal-margin expansion, higher realized prices, lower scrap costs and record shipments, plus a fabrication backlog nearly 50% above a year ago that extends into Q1 2027. Nucor expects steel mills earnings up on higher realized pricing across all major product categories with stable volumes. Both guides were reported below consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMC fell 3.83% to $64.53 on 2026-09-18, the session after both guides (MarketBeat quote page), so the sector's 'below consensus' reset has already been taken. No prior CMC reaction to peer guidance is in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline 'guided below consensus' was sold on 09-18 and the stock has not recovered (-1.65% over 20d). The positive content for CMC's margin and Q1 order book (SDI's lower scrap, strong orders, low customer inventories, record fab backlog) is a read-through the tape treated as a negative. If it had been priced as a positive, CMC would not sit at its September low.
findings.independence: Nucor guidance 8-K/PR of 2026-09-17 (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm) is a different company pointing the same way on pricing. The STLD 'lower-than-estimated' framing is from https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/stld-gets-street-backing-despite-lower-than-estimated-q3-guidance-wells-fargo-remains-constructive-on-margin-upside/cZtHbViRBE2

findings.finding: Into CMC's Q1 FY27 (Sep-Nov), the quarter the release will guide, Fastmarkets' 2026-09-30 survey points to US ferrous scrap up about 6.6% m/m in October (trend indicator 65.9) after +0.3% in September. GMK (2026-10-02) says imports capped US rebar increases in September, while beams and sections were raised $50/st from 1 October. Rising scrap with rebar lagging means a metal-margin squeeze on top of the usual seasonal Q1 step-down, against a management call in June that scrap would be 'fairly stable'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook-driven sell-offs: Oct 2025 -7.26% (Q4 FY25 print with Q1 outlook), Jan 2026 -3.56% (reported intraday -5.14% on a 'weak Q2 EBITDA outlook', https://www.itiger.com/news/1120498183), Mar 2026 -4.69%. CMC has sold three of its last four outlooks.
findings.why_not_priced: The October scrap settlement was still unagreed on 2026-10-09 (Fastmarkets delay notice), so the input-cost move is not yet a published number. Q1 FY27 consensus is not visible in any source read. If the squeeze were priced, the put skew would be the only sign of it, and that is on 495 contracts of OI.
findings.independence: GMK long-steel price roundup of 2026-10-02 (https://gmk.center/?p=129727) on imports capping rebar and beam increases. Partly offsetting: SDI's 09-17 guide expected lower scrap in Jul-Sep. This is macro-to-company transmission CMC has not confirmed, so it is a proxy and sized small.

findings.finding: Q3 Europe Steel adjusted EBITDA of $34.7m included a $20.4m CO2 credit. Management said reported Europe EBITDA falls in Q4 because the credit does not recur, even as operations improve modestly on the July 1 CBAM and safeguard changes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction to this line is recorded. It is inside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it was guided explicitly. The only residual is a headline EBITDA screen that does not adjust for the credit.
findings.independence: Q3 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). This shares the guide document with finding 1.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-05 the board added $600m to the repurchase authorization, taking it to about $717m (~10% of a ~$7.2bn market cap). The CFO said buybacks step up to 'more elevated levels' once net leverage reaches ~2x (2.1x at Q3), and FY27 capex was guided about $200m lower than FY26's ~$550m. Q4 buyback pace and any FY27 capital-return framing land in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned on capital return. Q3 repurchases were small ($18.9m).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public, but the pace is not. If Q4 shows sub-2x leverage and an accelerated cadence, it signals the FCF ramp the investor day promised for FY27. The stock trading 22% below its high suggests the market has not been paying for it.
findings.independence: Q3 call transcript on capex and the buyback trigger (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026).

findings.finding: Short interest built from ~4.7m shares (3.6 days, 2026-07-15) to 6.31m (5.16 days, ~5.7% of shares, 2026-09-30), and the put skew is +13.5 vol points, into a stock at its September lows and 22% off its 52-week high. Bearish positioning on the outlook is partly established, which gives a relief mechanism if the Q1 guide is merely seasonal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June 2026 print, after a weak spring, rose +3.94% despite a disputed EPS read. Not crowded enough (5.7%) for a squeeze-type move.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not information about the print. It is filed because it shapes the reaction function to an in-line outcome. Moderate size, so sized small.
findings.independence: Earlier settlement history at https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/. Skew from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Management kept FY26 precast adjusted EBITDA at $165-175m and called the precast backlog a record. It also guided Construction Solutions Group adjusted EBITDA up mid-teens sequentially in Q4 (from $97.4m, with precast at $52.9m), and said early-Q4 steel and precast shipments were strong after weather normalised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The precast acquisitions were part of the +3.94% June reaction. The segment is ~28% of core EBITDA and rising (investor day).
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the guide, so mostly priced. The residual is whether precast clears the top of the $165-175m range, which would support the investor-day plan for >40% CSG mix.
findings.independence: Q3 8-K release for the CSG mid-teens guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm). This shares the call document with findings 1 and 4.

outside_window.finding: Steel Dynamics reports Q3 on 2026-10-19 after close and Nucor on 2026-10-26 after close. Both peer prints land after CMC's exit window.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The put skew (+13.5) and the short build agree with my outlook-risk finding (scrap), while peer guidance and the capital-return path cut against the skew. The skew rests on a thin, wide chain, so it is weak evidence, and the net leans nothing.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series): the rebar price-trail finding (ChemAnalyst) was cut from -0.8 to -0.4, because Nucor's guide of higher realized pricing across all product categories is a broader counterparty statement pointing the other way.
Rule 3 (the caveat has to reach the number): the scrap/Q1-outlook finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.7, netting its own counterweight (October beam increases of +$50/st and SDI's lower Q3 scrap).
Rule 1 with rule 3: the peer-guidance positive was cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because the 09-18 -3.8% shows part of that information has already traded.

Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Europe CO2 finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, as it was explicitly guided. print_vs_bar moved from -1.0 to 0.0 once the bar was confirmed by two sources sitting on the company guide.
The pessimism-artefact note was checked: the post-lessons sum turns slightly positive (+0.3), while p_up stays 48 on the outlook-selling history and the skew.
